svg.title: What server-side tracking can and can't do
svg.desc: Two columns. It can: deliver events through your own domain, set longer-lived first-party cookies from the server, remove vendor scripts from the page, control what each vendor receives, send better match keys to ad platforms, and add a backend purchase source. It can't: bypass consent, fix broken or duplicate events, make every report agree, capture 100% of events, create sales on its own, or run for free.
svg.text: What server-side tracking can and can't do

g.text: Deliver events through your own domain
fewer requests lost to domain blocklists
Set first-party cookies from the server
often longer-lived than JavaScript cookies
Remove vendor scripts from the page
less third-party code in the browser
Control what each vendor receives
strip, hash or redact fields first
Send better match keys to ad platforms
hashed email/phone, fbp/fbc, event_id
Add a backend purchase source
orders recorded even if the thank-you page fails
Bypass consent
the same legal rules apply as for browser tags
Fix broken or duplicate events
it forwards whatever it receives
Make every report agree
platforms still attribute differently
Capture 100% of events
bots, network errors and early exits remain
Create sales on its own
better data, not better products or ads
Run for free
hosting plus setup and maintenance time

svg.text: How much each benefit helps depends on your audience, your current setup and how carefully the server container is configured.
